reference.title: Determination of post-perovskite phase transition boundary in MgSiO3 using Au and MgO pressure standards

source_location: Original full article, Table 1, all 13 rows; paragraphs 5-7 for thermometry and errors
recovery: Direct manual transcription of the original publisher HTML table, verified against table footnotes. This CSV is not a downloaded author file.

publisher_supplement.description: Publisher lists a 1012-byte tab-delimited Table 1. Retrieval returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-09; its contents and parity with the displayed table are unverified.

source_rounding: *_printed columns retain trailing zeros and parenthetical widths exactly. Plain numerical columns parse values and widths; cell volumes are derived a^3, and available volume errors are first-order 3*a^2*delta_a. Blank means unavailable, never zero.
zero_width_issue: Run 1 cycle 9 prints 3.7106(0). The printed token is retained; numerical uncertainty is blank rather than treating a rounded-to-zero width as exact knowledge.

pressure_scales.gold_tsuchiya_pressure_gpa: Tsuchiya (2003) Au EOS, as identified by the original table footnote; these values are retained but excluded as independent Au-fit targets.
pressure_scales.mgo_speziale_pressure_gpa: Speziale et al. (2001), DOI 10.1029/2000JB900318; only these reported targets are used for the Au thermal replay.

selection.thermal_replay: Run 2 cycles 1 and 2, the only heated rows with paired Au and MgO observations; identified explicitly in Fei (2007) Figure 1 caption.
selection.cold_comparison: Run 2 300 K row; no source error widths.
selection.excluded: All ten Run 1 rows lack MgO measurements, and using their Au-derived pressures to fit Au would be circular.

uncertainties.temperature_evidence: Paragraph 7: spatial variation within the 20 um diffraction area is less than +/-10% even at 2400 K. This is not a row-wise standard deviation. Pressure errors at high temperature derive mainly from temperature uncertainty; shared P-T covariance is not provided.

rights: No separate data license recovered. Original source rights remain with its rightsholders; no CC0 claim is made for the article or source table.
